jobs.description:
Description:

**Location**: Los Angeles, CA (50% travel)

**Position**: Full-Time

**Reports To**: Director of Customer Experience

TGR Solutions, Inc. designs and builds autonomous robots for regulated environments and is based in the heart of Los Angeles, California. TGR develops robotics solutions from the ground up and builds integrated systems that help organizations apply robotics and AI to demanding work.

TGR’s flagship product line, the A1 ADIBOT, is a fully autonomous UV-C disinfection robot that is deployed in facilities around the world. TGR team members come from diverse disciplines and backgrounds and share a hands-on approach to building robotics products.

**Job Description:**

The Implementation Specialist, Life Sciences brings ADIBOT autonomous UV-C disinfection robots into GMP environments and makes them part of how each site runs. A new robot in a classified area changes a validated state, so the job is as much about change control, qualification, and documentation as it is about operator training.

You will own each life sciences account on site from purchase order through its first 90 days. You will work with the customer's QA, Validation, Microbiology, Facilities, EHS, and Operations teams, and with TGR Customer Success, Technical Support, and Sales.

**Responsibilities:**

* Plan each deployment around the customer's contamination control strategy and change control process, so the robot enters the site as a documented, risk-assessed addition to its cleaning and disinfection program.
* Assess site readiness before delivery, including classified areas, airlocks, material transfer routes, doorways, charging, network access, and the rules for running cycles.
* Supply the technical package for the customer's change control: equipment description, UV-C safety data, and inputs to the risk assessment.
* Support the customer's QA team on site through IQ/OQ/PQ while they execute and approve the protocols.
* Become the subject matter expert on the robot and its disinfection protocols. Advise QA and Microbiology on available measurement options, such as dosimetry and cycle records, within TGR-approved claims, and supply robot cycle records for the validation package.
* Answer QA questions on how cycle records are generated, stored, and exported.
* Train and certify operators in UV-C safety, and help the customer write SOPs, work instructions, and training records.
* Review fleet data with each customer, resolve operational bottlenecks, and identify areas for expansion.
* Notify customers of firmware updates and support their change assessment before and after each update.
* Hand each account to Customer Success at day 90 with open items, training records, and a utilization baseline.
* Bring field learnings back to Product and Engineering.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, microbiology or biotechnology, or equivalent work experience.
* 2 to 4 years of field-based, customer-facing technical work, ideally in pharma, biotech, or medical device manufacturing.
* Working knowledge of gowning and work inside classified areas, plus ISO 14644, EU GMP Annex 1, and good documentation practice under GMP regulations.
* Experience with IQ/OQ/PQ and change control, whether you wrote, executed, or supported the protocols.
* Hands-on experience deploying or servicing complex machinery, and confidence troubleshooting hardware and software on site. Network troubleshooting experience is a plus.
* Familiarity with environmental monitoring and cleaning validation.
* Clear technical writing for SOPs, work instructions, and training records.
* Ability to travel 60%, including some weekends.

**Job Objective:**

  

Under the immediate direction of either the department Clinical Laboratory Scientist and the Senior Clinical Laboratory Scientist, or the Laboratory Phlebotomy/Processing Supervisor, the Laboratory Technician performs a variety of duties in the Clinical Laboratory including collecting and processing biological specimens, equipment operation, maintenance and calibration, preparing specimens to be sent to reference labs, monitoring special collection requirements, and assisting with orientation, training and competency. In addition, this person must also communicate with hospital staff by answering inquiries regarding test orders, specimen availability, and testing.

  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

**A.** **Technical**

* Organizes laboratory orders by priority and specimen type for proper collection and handling of specimens.
* Answers inquiries regarding test orders and specimen availability.
* Reports verified test results to physicians and nursing staff.
* Records temperatures and reports all out of range recordings.
* Maintains logs, worksheets, or charts as indicated by the department.

**B.** **Non-technica**l

* Operates the LIS, HIS and APS as required for the position.
* Demonstrates competence with computer downtime procedures.
* Resolves inquiries regarding pending orders and specimen availability.
* Assures that equipment, work surfaces, and glassware are cleaned daily.
* Completes inventory and organizes department supplies and reagents.
* Assists with orientation, training and competency evaluation as requested.
* Participates in Continuing Education for personal growth and maintenance of certificates and licenses.
* Assures completion of all yearly competency testing.

**C.** **Additional Duties**

* Department Technician
* Operates equipment and performs testing in assigned department within the scope of training and established protocols.
* Recognizes instrument malfunction and takes appropriate actions.
* Performs routine maintenance on equipment.

**Processing Technician**

* Assess workload and coordinates phlebotomy staffing assignments.
* Handles unique specimen collection requirements.
* Processes specimens for testing at selected reference laboratories.
* Packages specimens for special shipment.
* Processes 24-hour urine collections

**Pathology Technician**

* Process and send specimens for additional studies (bone marrow, cytogenetics, flow cytometry, etc.).
* Prepares and labels slides for pathologist review and keeps the process organized for pathologist.
* File Pathology slides and blocks in an organized fashion.
* Assist pathologist in cutting, staining and labeling frozen sections and rapid interpretations.
* Distribute and file pathology reports, orders, consultations, etc.
* Document all material received/released and returned.
* Interact with other departments within the hospital to resolve pathology matters.
* Respond to pathology-related calls and requests.
* Pick-up, accession, label and create cassettes for surgical, outpatient and cytological specimens.
* Register patients into hospital information system.
* Maintain integrity of patient information throughout processing.
* Set up grossing area for next day with supplies as needed.
* Assure proper maintenance of equipment (working with Biomed/Engineering/Vendors when needed), ordering/stocking of adequate supplies and cleanliness and organization of surgical pathology workstations (including cryostats and stain line) daily.
* Maintain cleanliness of grossing equipment.
* Filter/replace chemicals in stain line and maintain cleanliness of containers.
* Handle pathology specimens, cassettes and chemicals, including pouring formalin into specimen containers, as needed.
* Dispose of tissue and chemicals according to AVMC guidelines.
* Ensure proper identification of pathology specimens, including fetuses, as needed.
* Take specimens to radiology for imaging studies as needed.
* Assist with regulatory inspections and assignments as needed.
* Follow through with assigned projects.
* Support Pathology department as necessary.

**Non-Essential Duties:**

* Assists with routine phlebotomy as needed.
* Helps stock supplies in the various departments.
* Transports specimens and supplies between the main hospital lab and satellite locations.
* Adds support to other laboratory staff as necessary.

  

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

**Knowledge**

* Knowledge of basic computer operations.
* Knowledge of safe handling of biological specimens.
* Knowledge of specimen collection requirements.
* Knowledge to recognize deviations from normal standards.
* Demonstrates knowledge regarding special needs and behaviors of age specific groups and proficiency in required areas.

  

**Skills**

* Skill in performing venipuncture.
* Skill needed for accuracy and precision in processing specimens and testing.
* Effective oral and written communication skills.

**Abilities**

* Ability to follow directions accurately.
* Ability to learn specimen and testing requirements.
* Ability to learn requirements of operation for different types of instrumentation.
* Ability to recognize instrument malfunction and take appropriate action.
* Ability to operate Hospital and Laboratory Information Systems.
* Ability to use reference materials to locate information.
* Ability to exhibit courteous, helpful and professional behavior in dealing with patients, public and peers.

The Molecular Foundry at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is seeking a **Research Associate** to support its quantum research program through hands-on fabrication and characterization of superconducting devices. Working alongside experienced researchers, this individual will use advanced cleanroom equipment, help refine qubit fabrication processes, conduct experimental measurements, and contribute to scientific research aimed at advancing quantum technologies. This is an opportunity for an early-career technical professional to develop specialized nanofabrication skills within a collaborative national laboratory environment.

The Molecular Foundry is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science user facility that provides users from around the world with access to state-of-the-art expertise and instrumentation in nanoscale science. Joining our team means contributing directly to cutting-edge research in quantum materials and device engineering within a highly collaborative scientific community.

**You will:**

* Perform day-to-day fabrication of superconducting devices in support of the Foundry's quantum program.
* Support the development and refinement of recipe workflows for qubit fabrication.
* Work in a cleanroom environment using tools such as e-beam evaporators, scanning electron microscopes (SEM), lithography systems, and wet chemical benches.
* Assist with cryogenic characterization using a PPMS and dilution refrigerator to measure superconducting device performance metrics.
* Maintain accurate experimental records, sample tracking, and process documentation to support reproducibility across fabrication runs.

  

**We are looking for:**

* Bachelor’s degree in physics, engineering, materials science, or a related field preferred, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Demonstrated 1 year, hands-on experience in a research, laboratory, cleanroom, or related technical environment.

jobs.description:
### **About DeepOrigin**

Deep Origin is building ambitious science in a fast-moving environment, combining AI and physics-based methods with wet-lab biology to advance drug discovery. The people who thrive here are accountable, adaptable, rigorous, humble, and direct. Across roles, we look for:

* **Ownership through to the result.** An experiment isn't done until the data are analyzed, the conclusion is written down, and whoever needs it next has it.
* **Judgment under incomplete information.** You resolve what you need to know, commit to a defensible course of action, and revise when the evidence warrants it.
* **Exacting about the work, unguarded about yourself.** You hold data to a standard that survives scrutiny, and you drop your own interpretation when someone shows you better evidence.
* **Transparency as a working habit.** You surface problems while they are cheap to fix, and you explain your results so chemists, engineers, and computational colleagues can act on them.

### **About the role**

We are hiring a hands-on **Senior Research Associate** to build and run the cell-based assays and engineered cell lines behind our drug discovery programs. You will work day to day with a senior scientist in R&D, owning bench execution while helping shape assay strategy.

Your core work: maintaining mammalian cell lines, engineering them with RNP-based CRISPR (knockouts and knock-ins), generating validated stable lines, and turning them into robust functional assays. The data you generate feeds directly into AI and physics-based compound design, so quality and reproducibility matter as much as throughput.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

 **Requirements**  

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in biology, cell biology, bioengineering, biochemistry, immunology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Relevant hands-on laboratory experience
* Demonstrated mammalian cell culture experience with strong aseptic technique, including routine maintenance of multiple lines in parallel.
* Hands-on experience with CRISPR gene editing: knockout generation, and ideally knock-in, with validation of edited clones.
* Experience with transient transfection, and with generating and validating stable cell lines, including clonal selection and banking.
* Experience executing at least one cell-based assay readout, such as flow cytometry, plate-based viability, reporter, or proliferation assays.
* Ability to analyze data, assess assay quality, communicate findings clearly, and work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary setting.

Paleovalley and Wild Pastures were born from a simple but radical idea: real food can heal — people, animals, and the planet.
